overview.description: Coronary Artery Disease (CAD) is a condition where the major blood vessels supplying the heart (coronary arteries) become narrowed or blocked by plaque buildup (atherosclerosis). This limits blood flow to the heart muscle, causing chest pain (angina) or leading to a heart attack (myocardial infarction).
overview.prevalence: The most common type of heart disease; affects over 244 million people worldwide.
overview.age_group: Common in middle-aged and older adults, risk increases with age.

types.name: Stable Angina
types.description: Chest pain that occurs predictably during physical exertion or stress. Relieved by rest or nitroglycerin.
types.common_in: CAD patients with moderate arterial narrowing

types.name: Unstable Angina
types.description: Chest pain that occurs unexpectedly, even at rest. It is severe, lasts longer, and does not respond well to medication. It is a medical emergency.
types.common_in: Patients at immediate risk of heart attack

types.name: Microvascular Angina
types.description: Chest pain caused by spasms or blockages in the heart's smallest blood vessels rather than the main arteries.

severity_levels.name: Asymptomatic CAD
severity_levels.impact: Managed with lifestyle adjustments and cholesterol-lowering drugs

severity_levels.name: Chronic Stable Angina
severity_levels.frequency: Predictable chest pain during physical activity
severity_levels.impact: Requires daily medication (beta-blockers, nitroglycerin) to improve blood flow

severity_levels.name: Acute Coronary Syndrome (ACS) / Heart Attack
severity_levels.frequency: Sudden occlusion of a coronary artery leading to heart muscle damage
severity_levels.impact: CRITICAL EMERGENCY. Requires immediate angioplasty, thrombolytics, or bypass surgery

genetic_factors: Family history of early heart disease
Genetic predisposition to high blood pressure or hypercholesterolemia
environmental_triggers: Smoking and tobacco use (major risk factor)
Sedentary lifestyle and lack of physical exercise

primary_symptoms.name: Chest Pain (Angina)
primary_symptoms.description: Pressure, squeezing, fullness, or pain in the center of the chest. May feel like a heavy weight sitting on the chest.
primary_symptoms.onset: Triggered by exercise, stress, or cold weather

primary_symptoms.name: Shortness of Breath (Dyspnea)
primary_symptoms.description: Feeling winded or having difficulty catching breath, especially with physical exertion.

primary_symptoms.name: Pain Radiating to Arm, Neck, or Jaw
primary_symptoms.description: Discomfort that spreads from the chest to the left shoulder, left arm, neck, jaw, or back.

secondary_symptoms: Nausea, indigestion, or heartburn-like pain (more common in women)
warning_signs_of_attack: Chest pain/pressure lasting more than 5 minutes that does not go away with rest or nitroglycerin
Pain spreading to left shoulder, arm, throat, or jaw
Unexplained sweating combined with shortness of breath
Feeling of impending doom or panic
symptoms_in_children: Rare. Congenital coronary artery anomalies present with chest pain during competitive sports or feeding difficulties in infants

medical_history: Evaluation of symptom triggers, duration, and relief factors
Assessment of cardiovascular risk factors (diabetes, smoking)
physical_examination: Auscultation of heart sounds for murmurs or extra beats
Measuring blood pressure and heart rate

diagnostic_tests.description: Measures electrical activity of the heart.
diagnostic_tests.purpose: Detects ischemia, arrhythmia, or past heart attack patterns
diagnostic_tests.key_metric: ST-segment elevation or depression indicates active heart muscle distress

diagnostic_tests.purpose: Evaluates heart pumping efficiency (Ejection Fraction) and valve structure
diagnostic_tests.key_metric: Ejection Fraction < 50% indicates reduced heart function

diagnostic_tests.description: ECG monitoring while walking on a treadmill or under pharmacological stimulation.
Contrast dye is injected into arteries, and X-rays are taken to look for blockages.
diagnostic_tests.purpose: Gold standard for identifying exact locations of artery narrowing
diagnostic_tests.key_metric: Percentage blockage (> 70% narrowing is hemodynamically significant)

medicines.note: All medications should be taken only under the supervision of a licensed physician. Self-medication can be dangerous.

categories.purpose: Prevent blood clots from forming in narrowed coronary arteries, reducing heart attack risk

medicines.name: Aspirin (Low-Dose)
medicines.use_case: Primary and secondary prevention of cardiovascular events

medicines.name: Clopidogrel
medicines.use_case: Used in patients allergic to aspirin or after stent placement

categories.purpose: Relax and widen blood vessels, allowing more blood to reach the heart muscle and relieving chest pain

medicines.name: Nitroglycerin
medicines.dosage: 0.3-0.6 mg placed under the tongue during acute chest pain
medicines.use_case: Immediate relief of stable angina attacks

categories.purpose: Lower heart rate and blood pressure, reducing the heart's oxygen demand

diet_and_nutrition.overview: A heart-healthy diet prevents plaque progression and manages blood pressure and cholesterol levels.

items.benefit: Rich in monounsaturated fats that lower LDL (bad) cholesterol
Contain Omega-3 fatty acids and fiber that lower lipid counts
Soluble fiber binds to cholesterol in the digestive tract, preventing absorption

items.food: High-Sodium Foods (Processed meats, Pickles, Canned soups)
items.benefit: Sodium raises blood pressure, placing extra strain on coronary arteries

items.food: Trans Fats and Saturated Fats (Fried foods, Fatty red meats)
